common_name: Purple Viking Potato (Purple-Skinned White-Flesh Storage Potato)

planting.note: Plant certified seed pieces 4-6 weeks before last frost; in zone 9 plant January-February for harvest before summer heat sets in. Cut seed pieces to egg size with 1-2 eyes each and let cut surfaces cure a day or two before planting.

directions: Plant seed pieces 4 inches deep in loose, well-amended soil in full sun. Purple Viking produces large, oval tubers with striking purple-splashed pink skin over dense, moist, pure white flesh that holds together well when boiled, making it a favorite for potato salad as well as roasting and mashing. The vigorous plants are heavy yielders and the thick skin gives the tubers good storage life compared to thinner-skinned varieties. Hill soil around the stems as they emerge to keep developing tubers covered and prevent greening, and harvest after the vines die back for the best storage tubers.
sources: Texas A&M AgriLife Extension — Potato Production for Texas Home Gardens
University of Florida IFAS Extension — Potato Production in Florida

common_name: La Ratte Fingerling Potato (Classic French Gourmet Fingerling)

planting.note: Plant certified seed pieces 4-6 weeks before last frost; in zone 9 plant January-February for harvest before summer heat sets in. Cut seed pieces to egg size with 1-2 eyes each and let cut surfaces cure a day or two before planting.

directions: Plant seed pieces 4 inches deep in loose, well-amended soil in full sun. La Ratte is a classic French fingerling potato long prized by chefs for its exceptionally rich, nutty, almost chestnut-like flavor and dense, waxy, pale yellow flesh that holds its shape beautifully when boiled or roasted whole. The small, knobby, finger-shaped tubers mature over a somewhat longer season than standard round potatoes and yield less per plant, but the superior flavor has made it a long-standing favorite for specialty and high-end cooking. Harvest once vines begin to yellow and die back, and handle the thin-skinned tubers gently, since they bruise more easily than thicker-skinned storage potatoes.
sources: Texas A&M AgriLife Extension — Potato Production for Texas Home Gardens
University of Florida IFAS Extension — Potato Production in Florida

common_name: Carola Potato (German Waxy Yellow All-Purpose Potato)

planting.note: Plant certified seed pieces 4-6 weeks before last frost; in zone 9 plant January-February for harvest before summer heat sets in. Cut seed pieces to egg size with 1-2 eyes each and let cut surfaces cure a day or two before planting.

directions: Plant seed pieces 4 inches deep in loose, well-amended soil in full sun. Carola is a German-bred potato valued for its smooth, thin, light tan skin and dense, waxy, deep yellow flesh with rich, buttery flavor, performing well boiled, roasted, and in potato salads where a firm texture that holds together is wanted. It is a reliable, heavy-yielding variety with good resistance to common potato diseases and stores reasonably well after curing. Hill soil around the stems as they emerge, and harvest for storage after the vines have died back naturally.

Desiree is a widely grown Dutch-bred potato with smooth, rosy-red skin and pale yellow, moderately waxy flesh that holds its shape well when boiled, making it a versatile choice for roasting, salads, and general cooking. It is a vigorous, heavy-yielding variety with good tolerance for a range of soil conditions and reasonably good drought tolerance compared to some other cultivars. Hill soil around the stems as they emerge to prevent tubers from greening in the sun, and harvest for storage once the vines have died back naturally.
